items.title: The Problem of Pattern and Scale in Ecology: The Robert H. MacArthur Award Lecture
items.summary: It is argued that the problem of pattern and scale is the central problem in ecology, unifying population biology and ecosystems science, and marrying basic and applied ecology. Applied challenges, such as the prediction of the ecological causes and consequences of global climate change, require the interfacing of phenomena that occur on very different scales of space, time, and ecological organization. items.title: Molecular origami in neuroscience: noncanonical DNA structures and functional nucleic acids in neural regulation and disease
items.summary: Gliomas are increasingly recognized as network diseases in which aberrant interactions between tumor cells, neurons, and immune populations drive hyperexcitability, seizures, cognitive dysfunction, and disease progression. Simultaneously, advances in structural biology and nucleic acid engineering have revealed DNA to be a dynamic molecular architecture capable of sensing, regulating, and modulating cellular states. items.summary: Prior to the twentieth century, theories of knowledge were inherently perceptual. Since then, developments in logic, statistics, and programming languages have inspired amodal theories that rest on principles fundamentally different from those underlying perception. In addition, perceptual approaches have become widely viewed as untenable because they are assumed to implement recording systems, not conceptual systems. items.title: One-shot learning of paired association navigation with biologically plausible schemas
items.summary: After learning a multiple paired-association (MPA) navigation task, rodents can rapidly learn new cue–location associations after a single exposure, a phenomenon proposed to be facilitated by cognitive schemas. However, it remains unclear what schemas support this behavior and how they could be implemented in biological neural circuits. Here, we identify a set of schemas sufficient for gradual then one-shot paired-association navigation, and implement them in a fully neural agent using biologically plausible plasticity rules. Random-access laser-scanning optogenetics is a powerful and underutilized method for transiently manipulating cortical activity in mice. We identified a "salience network," anchored by dorsal anterior cingulate (dACC) and orbital frontoinsular cortices with robust connectivity to subcortical and limbic structures, and an "executive-control network" that links dorsolateral frontal and parietal neocortices. items.title: Loss of PAX6 alters the excitatory/inhibitory neuronal ratio in human cerebral organoids
items.summary: The transcription factor PAX6 is a crucial regulator of multiple aspects of embryonic forebrain development. It has well-established roles in the regulation of excitatory and inhibitory neuron development in the embryonic cortex in mice but PAX6's roles during human forebrain development are less well understood. Using human cerebral organoids, we investigated PAX6's roles in human neurodevelopment. items.title: Neural limits of temporal feature binding in human visual cortex
items.summary: Abstract Humans are able to track the change of color and orientation (CO) of an object at a stunning rate. However, spatially separating those features slows this rate by an order of magnitude – a temporal limit of feature binding that is little understood. Here, we investigate the underlying mechanisms using high-temporal resolution cortical source localization of the magnetic field response elicited by CO-pairs alternating at different frequencies in color and orientation. items.summary: Beyond motor control, the cerebellum has increasingly been implicated in cognitive functions, including inhibitory control, whereas its contribution to feedback-based associative learning remains less well established. items.summary: Introduction Sleep-disordered breathing (SDB) is highly prevalent after stroke and is associated with poor functional outcomes and increased mortality, yet systematic screening remains challenging because of limited polysomnography accessibility. We evaluated three electrocardiogram (ECG)-based indices for SDB screening in a large consecutive post-stroke cohort. items.title: Cell-type-specific localization of huntingtin-associated protein 1 in neuroendocrine and neurosecretory systems of the mouse hypothalamic–pituitary axis
items.summary: Huntingtin-associated protein 1 (HAP1) is a neurocytoplasmic protein implicated in intracellular trafficking, vesicular transport, and neuroprotection. Although HAP1 is abundantly expressed in hypothalamic regions involved in neuroendocrine regulation, its distribution and cellular specificity within the hypothalamic–pituitary axis remain poorly understood. Therefore, the present study aimed to characterize the expression pattern and cellular localization of HAP1 in neuroendocrine and neurosecretory systems of the adult mouse hypothalamic–pituitary axis. items.title: FieldTrip: Open Source Software for Advanced Analysis of MEG, EEG, and Invasive Electrophysiological Data
items.summary: This paper describes FieldTrip, an open source software package that we developed for the analysis of MEG, EEG, and other electrophysiological data. The software is implemented as a MATLAB toolbox and includes a complete set of consistent and user-friendly high-level functions that allow experimental neuroscientists to analyze experimental data. It includes algorithms for simple and advanced analysis, such as time-frequency analysis using multitapers, source reconstruction using dipoles, distributed sources and beamformers, connectivity analysis, and nonparametric statistical permutation tests

items.title: NRF2 signalling in environmental metal and metalloid neurotoxicity: distinguishing stress responses from functional neuroprotection
items.summary: Exposure to toxic metals and metalloids is an important public health concern because they can damage the nervous system and impair cognitive and motor function. Oxidative stress, disturbed glutathione balance, mitochondrial dysfunction and neuroinflammation are common features of this damage. items.title: Visualization of super-selective Wada with computed tomography perfusion: toward a novel option in preoperative functional mapping
items.summary: Introduction The Wada test has long been a well-established method for evaluating hemispheric dominance and functional localization; however, it has not been established as a visualizable functional imaging modality. Recently, the super-selective Wada test (ssWada) has emerged as a technique enabling more localized functional evaluation. By selectively catheterizing distal cerebral arterial branches, ssWada enables territory-based functional evaluation with higher spatial resolution than conventional approaches.
